cards.target: Ym mhen pum munud.
cards.english: In five minutes.

cards.target: Ym mhoced fy nghôt.
cards.english: In my coat pocket.
cards.existing: Three Welsh mutations: soft, nasal, aspirate. Nasal is rarest but appears after fy (my) and yn (in/at).

cards.target: Yr ail o Fehefin.
cards.english: The second of June.

cards.target: Bore da, shw' mae?
cards.english: Good morning, how are things?

cards.target: Mae'r siop gemydd fan hyn.
cards.english: The jeweller's is here.

cards.target: Difrodоdd y storm y to.
cards.english: The storm damaged the roof.

cards.target: Mae ei dad yn ffermwr.
cards.english: His father is a farmer.
cards.existing: Welsh changes the start of a word in many cases. cath → fy nghath (my cat) → ei gath (his cat). Three patterns: soft, nasal, aspirate.

cards.target: Mae tocynnau'n ddeg punt yr un.
cards.english: Tickets are ten pounds each.

cards.target: Mae'r canhwyllbren yn dal pum cannwyll.
cards.english: The candelabra holds five candles.

cards.target: Tu ôl i'r drws mae'r côt.
cards.english: Behind the door is the coat.
cards.existing: `'r` is the contracted definite article – happens after a vowel: `mae'r ci` (the dog is). Sticks to the preceding vowel.

cards.target: Prynhawn da, braf eich gweld chi.
cards.english: Good afternoon, nice to see you.
cards.existing: Possessive pronouns: `fy` (my), `dy` (your), `ei` (his/her), `ein` (our), `eich` (your pl), `eu` (their). Each triggers its own mutation on the noun.

cards.target: Mae'r ffaith bod e yma'n bwysig.
cards.english: The fact that he's here is important.

cards.target: Mae dwy bont dros yr afon.
cards.english: There are two bridges over the river.
cards.existing: Soft mutation: p→b, t→d, c→g, b→f, d→dd, m→f, ll→l. Trigger here: `dau` (two). After the number 2 the noun softens.

cards.target: Y gardd sy tu ôl i'r tŷ.
cards.english: It is the garden that is behind the house.
cards.existing: Welsh has multiple forms of 'the': `y` before consonants, `yr` before vowels, `'r` after vowels in the previous word. `Mae'r ci` vs `mae yr afal` (the apple is).

cards.target: Mae'r ysgol y tu ôl i'r eglwys.
cards.english: The school is behind the church.

cards.target: Mae e'n rhedeg tair milltir bob dydd.
cards.english: He runs three miles every day.

cards.target: Dw i'n ffonio fy rhieni bob wythnos.
cards.english: I phone my parents every week.

cards.target: Mae ei fam-gu yn naw deg oed.
cards.english: His grandmother is ninety years old.

cards.target: Dw i'n teimlo'n hapus heddiw, diolch byth.
cards.english: I feel happy today, thank goodness.

cards.target: Dw i'n deffro am saith bob bore.
cards.english: I wake up at seven every morning.

cards.target: Gallwn ni gerdded yno mewn deg munud.
cards.english: We can walk there in ten minutes.
cards.existing: Number agreement is singular: `pum afal` (five apples – apple stays singular!). Welsh, like many languages, counts on a singular noun after the number.

cards.target: Bore da bawb, croeso i'r dosbarth heddiw.
cards.english: Good morning everyone, welcome to class today.
cards.existing: After consonants, the article is `y`: `y dyn` (the man), `y plant` (the children). Before vowels (including 'h'), `yr`: `yr afal`, `yr hen`.

cards.target: Dydyn ni ddim angen unrhyw help, diolch.
cards.english: We don't need any help, thank you.

cards.target: Dw i ddim yn gallu ffeindio fy ffôn.
cards.english: I can't find my phone.

cards.target: Mae pob taith yn dechrau gydag un cam.
cards.english: Every journey begins with one step.

cards.target: Mae fy nheulu i'n byw yn y gogledd.
cards.english: My family lives in the north.

cards.target: Mae angen batri newydd ar ei gar e.
cards.english: His car needs a new battery.

cards.target: Mae'r cyfarfod yn dechrau am chwarter wedi dau.
cards.english: The meeting starts at quarter past two.

cards.target: Mae'r plant wrth eu bodd yn ymweld â'u nain.
cards.english: The children are delighted to visit their grandmother.

cards.target: Mae'r trên yn gadael am hanner awr wedi naw.
cards.english: The train leaves at half past nine.

cards.target: Mae'r cloc taid yn taro deuddeg bob hanner nos.
cards.english: The grandfather clock strikes twelve every night at midnight.

cards.target: Mae teithio'n ehangu'r meddwl.
cards.english: Travelling broadens the mind.

cards.target: Mae Cymru'n arwain ar ailgylchu.
cards.english: Wales leads on recycling.

cards.target: Gwlad y gân yw Cymru.
cards.english: Wales is the land of song.

cards.target: Mae'r adar uwchben y toeau.
cards.english: The birds are above the rooftops.

cards.target: Helo, fy enw i ydy Siân.
cards.english: Hello, my name is Siân.
cards.existing: Mutation by possessive: `fy` (nasal), `dy/ei-his` (soft), `ei-her/eu` (aspirate), `ein/eich` (none). The same pattern = different meanings.

cards.target: Mae toiledau ar y llawr cyntaf.
cards.english: Toilets are on the first floor.

cards.target: Gwylion ni'r gêm rygbi ddydd Sadwrn.
cards.english: We watched the rugby match on Saturday.

cards.target: Cenir y gân mewn gemau rygbi.
cards.english: The song is sung at rugby matches.

cards.target: Mae'r haf yn gynhesach na'r gwanwyn.
cards.english: The summer is warmer than the spring.

cards.target: Mae tair eglwys yn y dref.
cards.english: There are three churches in the town.

cards.target: Mae tri pheth ar y rhestr.
cards.english: There are three things on the list.
cards.existing: Aspirate mutation: p→ph, t→th, c→ch – happens after `ei` (her), `tri`, `chwe`, `a` (and), `â` (with). `Cath → ei chath` (her cat).

cards.target: Gwerthusir y rhaglen bob tair blynedd.
cards.english: The programme is evaluated every three years.

cards.target: Mae'r ardd o flaen y tŷ.
cards.english: The garden is in front of the house.

cards.target: Mae poblogaeth Cymru tua thair miliwn.
cards.english: Wales has a population of about three million.

cards.target: Mae gwylio Sianel Pedwar Cymru yn helpu.
cards.english: Watching Channel Four Wales helps.

cards.target: Mae'r bwtres yn cynnal wal yr eglwys.
cards.english: The buttress supports the church wall.

cards.target: Mae'r cogydd yn paratoi cawl cennin traddodiadol.
cards.english: The chef prepares traditional leek soup.

cards.target: Mae'r murlun yn addurno wal yr ysgol.
cards.english: The mural decorates the school wall.

cards.target: Mae'r ci y tu mewn i'r cwt.
cards.english: The dog is inside the kennel.

cards.target: Mae'r car y tu allan i'r garej.
cards.english: The car is outside the garage.

cards.target: Dy awgrym di oedd yr un gorau.
cards.english: Your suggestion was the best one.

cards.target: Dw i'n yfed wyth gwydraid y dydd.
cards.english: I drink eight glasses a day.

cards.target: Mae ei mam hi'n pobi'r bara gorau.
cards.english: Her mother bakes the best bread.

cards.target: Mwynhaon ni'r tân gwyllt noson Guto Ffowc.
cards.english: We enjoyed the fireworks on bonfire night.

cards.target: Dawnsiwch gyda mi yn y neuadd heno!
cards.english: Dance with me in the hall tonight!
cards.existing: Common polite request structure: imperative + `os gwelwch yn dda` (please). `Eisteddwch, os gwelwch yn dda` (Please sit down).

cards.target: Mae'r awyr yn lanach yng nghefn gwlad.
cards.english: The air is cleaner in the countryside.

cards.target: Mae e wedi rhedeg tri marathon eleni.
cards.english: He has run three marathons this year.

cards.target: Mae tŵr cloc yng nghanol y dref.
cards.english: There is a clock tower in the centre of town.
cards.existing: Nasal mutation makes voiced stops nasal: b→m, d→n, g→ng. Hardest to spot – the consonant looks like a different letter.

cards.target: Mae'r lloeren yn cylchdroi o amgylch y Ddaear.
cards.english: The satellite orbits around the Earth.

cards.target: Mae'r ongl sgwâr yn mesur naw deg gradd.
cards.english: The right angle measures ninety degrees.

cards.target: Mae fy ewythr yn ffermio yng ngogledd Cymru.
cards.english: My uncle farms in north Wales.
cards.existing: yn becomes ym before m, yng before ng. Yn Caerdydd → yng Nghaerdydd (in Cardiff). Spelling tracks the sound.

cards.target: Mae Cymraeg yn un o fy hoff bynciau.
cards.english: Welsh is one of my favourite subjects.

cards.target: Adeiladwyd y castell ym mil dau wyth tri.
cards.english: The castle was built in twelve eighty-three.

cards.target: Adeiladwyd yr ysgol ym mil naw pump dau.
cards.english: The school was built in nineteen fifty-two.

cards.target: Mae ei frawd e'n chwarae i'r tîm cenedlaethol.
cards.english: His brother plays for the national team.

cards.target: Mae ei weithdy e yn yr hen sgubor.
cards.english: His workshop is in the old barn.

cards.target: Mae'r llyfrgell ar agor o naw tan bump.
cards.english: The library is open from nine to five.

cards.target: Mae'r gacen hon yn well na'r un ddiwethaf.
cards.english: This cake is better than the last one.

cards.target: Mae ei chwaer yn nyrs yn yr ysbyty.
cards.english: Her sister is a nurse at the hospital.

cards.target: Mae ei garedigrwydd yn adnabyddus yn y pentref.
cards.english: His kindness is well known in the village.

cards.target: Mae fy ffrind gorau fel chwaer i fi.
cards.english: My best friend is like a sister to me.

cards.target: Mae tri deg un o ddiwrnodau ym mis Mawrth.
cards.english: There are thirty-one days in March.

cards.target: Allwch chi siarad yn arafach, os gwelwch yn dda?
cards.english: Can you speak more slowly, please?
cards.existing: Imperative ending `-wch` is formal/plural: `Eisteddwch` (sit down), `Cymerwch` (take), `Edrychwch` (look). Use this with `chi` (formal/group address).

cards.target: Rydyn ni wedi mynychu pob gêm y tymor hwn.
cards.english: We have attended every match this season.

cards.target: Mae'r blwch post y tu allan i'r swyddfa bost.
cards.english: The postbox is outside the post office.
cards.existing: Negative imperative uses `peidiwch â + verb-noun` (don't): `Peidiwch â mynd` (don't go). For informal singular: `Paid â mynd`.

cards.target: Mae'r trên yn cyrraedd am ugain munud i bedwar.
cards.english: The train arrives at twenty to four.

cards.target: Oes bwydlen Gymraeg gyda chi, os gwelwch yn dda?
cards.english: Do you have a Welsh menu, please?
cards.existing: Singular/informal imperative drops the ending or uses the bare stem: `Eistedd!`, `Cymer!`, `Edrych!`. Compare to plural/formal `-wch`.

cards.target: Dw i'n mynd i'r gwaith bob bore am wyth.
cards.english: I go to work every morning at eight.

cards.target: Dw i'n hoffi darllen llyfrau yn fy amser sbâr.
cards.english: I like reading books in my spare time.

cards.target: Hoffwn i dalu'r bil nawr, os gwelwch yn dda.
cards.english: I'd like to pay the bill now, please.
cards.existing: Compact alternative: `Hoffwn i ...` (I would like to ...) – `hoffwn` already has the conditional baked in. Common in polite requests.

cards.target: Mae'r pellter rhwng y ddwy dref yn ugain milltir.
cards.english: The distance between the two towns is twenty miles.

cards.target: Mae Dydd Gŵyl Dewi ar y cyntaf o Fawrth.
cards.english: St David's Day is on the first of March.

cards.target: Mae fy mab yn gweithio mewn ysbyty fel meddyg.
cards.english: My son works in a hospital as a doctor.

cards.target: Dw i wedi bod yn dysgu Cymraeg ers dwy flynedd.
cards.english: I have been learning Welsh for two years.
cards.existing: Numbers from 2 onwards have masc/fem forms. `dau gi` (2 m. dogs) vs `dwy gath` (2 f. cats). The noun soft-mutates either way.

cards.target: Dal ati i symud ymlaen, un cam ar y tro.
cards.english: Keep moving forward, one step at a time.

cards.target: Mae e wedi dysgu yn yr ysgol ers deng mlynedd.
cards.english: He has been teaching at the school for ten years.

cards.target: Mae fy nhrefn foreol yn dechrau gyda phaned o de.
cards.english: My morning routine starts with a cup of tea.

cards.target: Mae gennym ni gi a dwy gath yn y tŷ.
cards.english: We have a dog and two cats in the house.
cards.existing: Numbers from 2 onwards have masc/fem forms. `dau gi` (2 m. dogs) vs `dwy gath` (2 f. cats). The noun soft-mutates either way.

cards.target: Mae tri chant chwe deg pump o ddyddiau mewn blwyddyn.
cards.english: There are three hundred and sixty-five days in a year.
cards.existing: Aspirate mutation: p→ph, t→th, c→ch – happens after `ei` (her), `tri`, `chwe`, `a` (and), `â` (with). `Cath → ei chath` (her cat).

cards.target: Mae gen i boen yn fy mhen ers y bore.
cards.english: I've had a pain in my head since this morning.

cards.target: Mae fy mam-gu'n byw ar ei phen ei hun mewn bwthyn.
cards.english: My grandmother lives alone in a cottage.

cards.target: Mae angen i ni fod yno erbyn hanner awr wedi naw.
cards.english: We need to be there by half past nine.

cards.target: Mae ei fferm e wedi bod yn y teulu ers cenedlaethau.
cards.english: His farm has been in the family for generations.

cards.target: Y cyntaf o Fawrth yw'r diwrnod pwysicaf yn y calendr Cymreig.
cards.english: The first of March is the most important day in the Welsh calendar.

cards.target: Mae'r Gŵyl Ddewi yn cael ei dathlu ar y cyntaf o Fawrth.
cards.english: St David's Day is celebrated on the first of March.

cards.target: Os cofiaf yn iawn, mae'r cyngerdd yn dechrau am hanner awr wedi saith yr hwyr.
cards.english: If I remember correctly, the concert starts at half past seven in the evening.

cards.target: Mae cerdded yn y mynyddoedd yn un o'r gweithgareddau awyr agored mwyaf poblogaidd yng Nghymru.
cards.english: Walking in the mountains is one of the most popular outdoor activities in Wales.
cards.existing: yn becomes ym before m, yng before ng. Yn Caerdydd → yng Nghaerdydd (in Cardiff). Spelling tracks the sound.

cards.target: Mae pobl yn gwisgo cennin Pedr ar eu cotiau i ddathlu Dydd Gŵyl Dewi ar y cyntaf o Fawrth.
cards.english: People wear daffodils on their coats to celebrate Saint David's Day on the first of March.

cards.target: Mewn cerddoriaeth, mae fortissimo yn golygu chwarae'n uchel iawn ac yn cael ei farcio â dwy ff ar y sgôr.
cards.english: In music, fortissimo means playing very loudly and is marked with two letter effs on the score.
cards.existing: `Cael` = 'to get, receive'. Used to build the passive: `Cafodd y llyfr ei brynu` (the book was bought). Literally 'got its buying'.

cards.target: Mae'r camlas yn cysylltu'r ddwy afon.
cards.english: The canal connects the two rivers.

cards.target: Mae'r darlith yn esbonio damcaniaeth esblygiad.
cards.english: The lecture explains the theory of evolution.

cards.target: Mae'r hologram yn dangos delwedd tri dimensiwn.
cards.english: The hologram shows a three-dimensional image.

cards.target: Mae'r heneb yn coffáu'r rhyfel byd cyntaf.
cards.english: The memorial commemorates the first world war.

cards.target: Mae'r celfyddydau'n chwarae rhan bwysig mewn cymdeithas.
cards.english: The arts play an important role in society.

cards.target: Mae'r cyfryngau'n chwarae rôl hanfodol mewn democratiaeth.
cards.english: The media plays a crucial role in democracy.

cards.target: O flaen yr orsaf mae tacsi.
cards.english: In front of the station is a taxi.

cards.target: Mae'r hamacan yn siglo rhwng y ddwy goeden.
cards.english: The hammock swings between the two trees.

cards.target: Mae'r platypws yn un o'r mamaliaid mwyaf rhyfedd.
cards.english: The platypus is one of the strangest mammals.

cards.target: Mae'r Nîl yn un o afonydd hiraf y byd.
cards.english: The Nile is one of the longest rivers in the world.

cards.target: Cyflwynwyd y wobr gyntaf i'r enillydd gan y maer yn neuadd y dref.
cards.english: The first prize was presented to the winner by the mayor at the town hall.

cards.target: Mae buddsoddi mewn ynni adnewyddadwy yn hanfodol os yw Cymru am gyrraedd ei thargedau hinsawdd erbyn dau ddeg pump deg.
cards.english: Investment in renewable energy is essential if Wales is to meet its climate targets by 2050.
cards.existing: Aspirate is the easiest to spot – words start with `ch`, `ph`, or `th`. If you see those, the trigger is usually one of: `ei` (her), `tri`, `chwe`, `a`/`â`.

cards.target: Sut wyt ti?
cards.english: How are you?
